import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Create a figure with subplots for comprehensive customer segmentation analysis
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 3, hspace=0.3, wspace=0.3)

# Calculate total spending and age
df['TotalSpending'] = (df['MntWines'] + df['MntFruits'] + df['MntMeatProducts'] + 
                       df['MntFishProducts'] + df['MntSweetProducts'] + df['MntGoldProds'])
df['Age'] = 2024 - df['Year_Birth']

# 1. Income Distribution by Education (top left)
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
education_order = df.groupby('Education')['Income'].median().sort_values(ascending=False).index
sns.boxplot(data=df, y='Education', x='Income', order=education_order, palette='Set2', ax=ax1)
ax1.set_title('Income Distribution by Education Level', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_ylabel('Education', fontsize=10)

# 2. Total Spending vs Income (top middle)
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
scatter = ax2.scatter(df['Income'], df['TotalSpending'], 
                     c=df['Age'], cmap='viridis', alpha=0.6, s=30)
ax2.set_title('Spending vs Income (colored by Age)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Income ($)', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Total Spending ($)', fontsize=10)
cbar = plt.colorbar(scatter, ax=ax2)
cbar.set_label('Age', fontsize=9)

# 3. Product Category Spending (top right)
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 2])
product_spending = {
    'Wines': df['MntWines'].sum(),
    'Meat': df['MntMeatProducts'].sum(),
    'Fish': df['MntFishProducts'].sum(),
    'Fruits': df['MntFruits'].sum(),
    'Sweets': df['MntSweetProducts'].sum(),
    'Gold': df['MntGoldProds'].sum()
}
colors = plt.cm.Set3(range(len(product_spending)))
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax3.pie(product_spending.values(), labels=product_spending.keys(), 
                                     autopct='%1.1f%%', colors=colors, startangle=90)
ax3.set_title('Total Spending by Product Category', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('black')
    autotext.set_fontsize(9)

# 4. Purchase Channel Distribution (middle left)
ax4 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
channels = ['Web', 'Catalog', 'Store', 'Deals']
channel_counts = [df['NumWebPurchases'].sum(), df['NumCatalogPurchases'].sum(), 
                  df['NumStorePurchases'].sum(), df['NumDealsPurchases'].sum()]
bars = ax4.bar(channels, channel_counts, color=['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4', '#45B7D1', '#FFA07A'])
ax4.set_title('Total Purchases by Channel', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Purchases', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_xlabel('Channel', fontsize=10)
for bar in bars:
    height = bar.get_height()
    ax4.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height,
            f'{int(height):,}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# 5. Campaign Response Rate (middle middle)
ax5 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
campaigns = ['Cmp1', 'Cmp2', 'Cmp3', 'Cmp4', 'Cmp5', 'Response']
response_rates = [
    df['AcceptedCmp1'].mean() * 100,
    df['AcceptedCmp2'].mean() * 100,
    df['AcceptedCmp3'].mean() * 100,
    df['AcceptedCmp4'].mean() * 100,
    df['AcceptedCmp5'].mean() * 100,
    df['Response'].mean() * 100
]
bars = ax5.barh(campaigns, response_rates, color='steelblue')
ax5.set_title('Campaign Response Rates', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax5.set_xlabel('Response Rate (%)', fontsize=10)
for i, (bar, rate) in enumerate(zip(bars, response_rates)):
    ax5.text(rate + 0.3, i, f'{rate:.1f}%', va='center', fontsize=9)

# 6. Family Composition (middle right)
ax6 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 2])
df['TotalKids'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']
kids_spending = df.groupby('TotalKids')['TotalSpending'].mean()
ax6.plot(kids_spending.index, kids_spending.values, marker='o', linewidth=2, 
         markersize=8, color='darkgreen')
ax6.set_title('Average Spending by Number of Children', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax6.set_xlabel('Number of Children at Home', fontsize=10)
ax6.set_ylabel('Average Total Spending ($)', fontsize=10)
ax6.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

# 7. Age Distribution (bottom left)
ax7 = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
ax7.hist(df['Age'], bins=30, color='coral', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
ax7.axvline(df['Age'].mean(), color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=2, label=f'Mean: {df["Age"].mean():.1f}')
ax7.set_title('Customer Age Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax7.set_xlabel('Age (years)', fontsize=10)
ax7.set_ylabel('Frequency', fontsize=10)
ax7.legend(fontsize=9)

for i, (status, value) in enumerate(marital_spending.items()):
